42:7: God Almighty says, as We revealed to the prophets before you, We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur’an, meaning clear, distinct, and obvious, that you may warn the Mother of Towns, which is Mecca, and those around it, meaning all the lands east and west. 42:13: God says to this nation: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad] So He mentioned the first of the messengers after Adam, peace be upon him, which is Noah, peace be upon him, and the last of them is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He mentioned among them those of strong resolve, which are Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary. This verse includes the mention of the five, just as the verse of Al-Ahzab included them in His statement, the Most High: And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary The verse. The religion that all the messengers brought is the worship of God alone, with no partner or associate, as God, the Almighty, said: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, 'There is no deity except Me, so worship Me.' In the hadith: We, the prophets, are children of one religion, meaning the common denominator among them is the worship of God alone, with no partner or associate, even if their laws and methods differed, as God, the Almighty, says: To each among you We prescribed a law and a method. That is why God, the Almighty, says here: Establish the religion and do not be divided therein, meaning God, the Almighty, commanded all the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, to unite and be united. And He forbade them from division and disagreement. God, the Almighty, says: Grievous is that to which you invite them, meaning it was difficult for them and they rejected what you, O Muhammad, invite them to of monotheism. Then He, the Most High, said: God chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]. That is, He is the One who decrees guidance for those who deserve it and decrees misguidance for those who choose it over the path of righteousness. For this reason, the Most High said: And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them. That is, their opposition to the truth came after it had reached them and the proof had been established against them. What drove them to do that was nothing but transgression, stubbornness, and hardship. Then the Most High said: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term. That is, had it not been for the previous word from God, the Most High, to grant the servants respite by establishing their account until the Day of Judgment, He would have hastened the punishment upon them in this world quickly. And His, the Most High, said: And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them, meaning the later generation after the first century that denied the truth, are in disquieting doubt about it. That is, they are not certain about their matter and faith, but rather they imitate their fathers and forefathers without proof or evidence, and they are confused about their matter, disquieting doubt, and widespread dissension.

God the Almighty said: God is our Lord and your Lord, meaning, He is the One Who is worshipped, there is no god but Him. We acknowledge this by choice, and even if you do not do it by choice, everyone in the world prostrates to Him willingly and by choice. God the Almighty said: For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds, meaning, we are innocent of you, as He the Almighty said: "But if they deny you, then say, 'For me is my work, and for you is your work. As-Suddi said: This was before the revelation of the verse of the sword, and this is correct because this verse was revealed in Mecca, and the verse of the sword was revealed after the Hijra. And the Almighty’s saying: God will gather us together meaning on the Day of Resurrection, like His saying: “Say: Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us in truth. 42:16: God the Almighty says, threatening those who turn away from the path of God those who believe in Him: And those who dispute about God after it has been responded to meaning they argue with the believers who responded to God and His Messenger to turn them away from the path of guidance they have taken their argument is invalid with their Lord meaning it is invalid with God and upon them is wrath meaning from Him and for them is a severe punishment meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and Mujahid said: They argued with the believers after they responded to God and His Messenger to turn them away from guidance and they hoped that ignorance would return. Qatadah said: They are the Jews and Christians who said: Our religion is better than your religion and our Prophet was before your Prophet and we are better than you and closer to God than you. But they lied about that. Then the Almighty said: It is God who sent down the Book in truth, meaning the books sent down from Him to His prophets, and the balance, which is justice and fairness, as Mujahid and Qatadah said. This is like the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the balance that people may maintain justice, and His saying: And the heaven He raised and set up the balance, so that you may not transgress within the balance, and establish weight in justice and do not make deficient the balance. God the Almighty says: And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. This includes encouragement and warning against it, and a disdain for this world. God the Almighty says: Those who do not believe in it urge it on. That is, they say, When will this promise come, if you are truthful? They only say that out of denial, rejection, disbelief, and stubbornness. But those who believe are fearful of it. That is, they are afraid and apprehensive of its occurrence. And they know that it is the truth. That is, it will inevitably happen, so they are prepared for it and working for it. It has been narrated through chains of transmission that reach the level of mutawatir in the Sahihs, Hassans, Sunans, and Musnads. Some of the wordings state that a man asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a loud voice while he was on one of his travels. He called out to him, saying, O Muhammad! The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him in a voice similar to his own: Come! The man asked him, When will the Hour come? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Woe to you! It will happen, so what have you prepared for it? He said: The love of God and His Messenger. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You will be with those you love. His saying in the hadith, A person will be with those he loves, is undoubtedly mutawatir. The point is that he did not answer him about the time of the Hour, but rather ordered him to prepare for it. God the Almighty said: Unquestionably, those who dispute about the Hour meaning, they argue about its existence and deny its occurrence are in far error meaning, in clear ignorance, because the One who created the heavens and the earth is able to revive the dead in a more appropriate and appropriate way, as God the Almighty said: And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him.

42:19: God Almighty says, informing us of His kindness to His creation in His provision for them, one after the other, not forgetting any of them, whether they are righteous or wicked, as in His saying, the Almighty: “And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.” And there are many similar examples. And His saying, the Almighty and Majestic: He provides for whom He wills, meaning He gives abundantly to whom He wills. And He is the Strong, the Exalted in Might, meaning nothing is beyond His power. Then God Almighty said: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, meaning the work of the Hereafter, We will increase for him in his harvest, meaning We will strengthen him and help him in what he is doing and increase his growth and reward him for the good deed ten times as much to seven hundred times as much, to whatever God wills. And whoever desires the harvest of this world, We will give him thereof, and he will have no share in the Hereafter, meaning whoever only strives to obtain something from this world and has no concern for the Hereafter at all, God will deprive him of the Hereafter and this world, if He wills. He gave him from it, and if he did not want it, he would not get either of them. The one who strives with this intention wins the losing deal in this world and the hereafter. The evidence for this is that this verse here is linked to the verse in Subhan, which is the saying of God, the Most High: “Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him from it what We will for whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will burn, blamed and banished. But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer - it is those whose effort is ever appreciated. No, these and those We give from the gift of your Lord, and the gift of your Lord is not restricted. See how We have preferred some of them over others, and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference.” Al-Thawri said on the authority of Mughirah on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Give this nation good tidings of glory, elevation, victory, and empowerment on earth. Whoever among them does the work of the Hereafter for the sake of this world will have no share in the Hereafter.” And the words of God Almighty: Or have they partners who have instituted for them a religion with which God has not given permission? That is, they do not follow what God has instituted for you of the correct religion, rather they follow what their devils from among the jinn and mankind have instituted for them of prohibiting what they have forbidden to them of the bahīrah, the sa’ibah, the wasīlah, and the ham, and permitting the eating of dead meat, blood, and gambling, and other such false misguidance and ignorance that they had invented in their pre-Islamic period of permitting and prohibiting, false worship, and corrupt statements. It has been proven in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Amr ibn Luhay ibn Qam’ah dragging his intestines in the Fire, because he was the first to let the sa’ibah go free. This man was one of the kings of Khuza’ah, and he was the first to do these things, and he is the one who forced the Quraysh to worship…” Idols are cursed and made ugly by God. That is why God Almighty said: And had it not been for the decisive word, the matter would have been decided between them. That is, they would have been hastened to receive punishment had it not been for the postponement until the Day of Resurrection. And indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment. That is, severe and painful in Hell, and what an evil destination. Then God the Almighty said: You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned meaning in the arenas of the Resurrection and it will inevitably befall them meaning what they fear will inevitably befall them. This is their state on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be in this state of fear and dread. And those who have believed and done righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise, having whatever they wish with their Lord How does this compare to this? How does one who is in the arenas of humiliation, disgrace, and certain fear because of his wrongdoing compare to one who is in the gardens of Paradise, enjoying whatever he wishes of food, drink, clothing, dwellings, sights, marriages, and pleasures that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man? Al-Hasan ibn Arafa said: Amr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Abbar told us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Abu Taybah, who said: The people of Paradise will drink from a cloud that will shade them, and it will say, What has rained upon you? He said: No one among the people will supplicate for anything except that it will rain upon them, to the point that one of them will say, We have been rained upon by virgins of equal age. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Arafa, and that is why God Almighty said: That is the great bounty, meaning the great victory and the complete, comprehensive, and universal blessing.

42:23: God the Almighty says when He mentioned the gardens of Paradise, for His servants who believed and did righteous deeds, That is what God gives good tidings to His servants who believed and did righteous deeds. That is, this will inevitably happen to them through God’s good tidings to them. And His Almighty saying, Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.’ That is, say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists from the disbelievers of Quraysh, “I do not ask of you for this message and advice what you will not give me. Rather, I ask of you to refrain from your evil toward me and leave me to deliver the messages of my Lord. If you do not support me, then do not harm me because of the kinship between me and you.” Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Abd al-Malik ibn Maisarah, who said: I heard Tawus narrating on the authority of Ibn `Abbas may God be pleased with them both that he was asked about the verse, Except for the affection of kinship. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: The kinship of the family of Muhammad. Ibn `Abbas said: “You are hasty. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did not have a clan of Quraysh except that he had kinship with them.” He said: Except that you do not maintain kinship ties between me and you. Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it, and Imam Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Qattan narrated it on the authority of Shu`bah. `Amir al-Sha`bi, al-Dahhak, `Ali ibn Abi Talhah, al-`Awfi, Yusuf ibn Mihran, and others narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn `Abbas may God be pleased with them both. Mujahid, `Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Abu Malik, `Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others said the same. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim bin al-Qasim bin Zaid al-Tabarani and Ja’far al-Qalanisi told us: Adam bin Abi Iyas told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I do not ask of you any reward for it except that you love me for my sake because of my kinship to you and that you preserve the kinship that is between me and you. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Hasan bin Musa, Qaz’ah, meaning Ibn Suwayd bin Abi Hatim, told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muslim bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Qaz’ah bin Suwayd, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not ask of you any reward for what I have given you of clear proofs and guidance except that you love God and draw near to Him by obeying Him. Qatadah narrated something similar on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri. This is as if it is an explanation of a second statement, as if he is saying, except for love for kinship, meaning, that you do the acts of obedience that will bring you nearer to God. A third statement is what Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, meaning that he said: The meaning of this is that you should treat me kindly among your relatives, meaning that you should be good to them and be righteous towards them. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Al-Daylam who said: When Ali bin Al-Hussein may God be pleased with him was brought as a prisoner and was placed on the steps of Damascus, a man from the people of Ash-Sham stood up and said: Praise be to God who killed you, uprooted you, and cut off the horn of sedition. Ali bin Al-Hussein may God be pleased with him said to him: Have you recited the Qur’an? He said: Yes. He said: Have you recited Al-Ha Meem? He said: I recited the Qur’an but I did not recite Al-Ha Meem. He said: “What did you recite: ‘Say, “I do not ask of you any reward for this but the love of my relatives.”’ He said: And you are they? He said: Yes. Abu Ishaq Al-Subaie said: “I asked Amr bin Shuaib about the words of God the Most High: ‘Say, “I do not ask of you any reward for this but the love of my relatives.”’ He said: “The relatives of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him).” Both were narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Malik bin Ismail told us, Abd al-Salam told us, Yazid bin Abi Ziyad told me, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Ansar said: We did this and that, and it was as if they were boasting. Then Ibn Abbas or al-Abbas, may God be pleased with them both - Abd al-Salam was unsure - said: We have the advantage over you. report of that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he came to them in their gatherings and said: O group of Ansar, were you not humble and then God honored you through me? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Were you not astray and then God guided you through me? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Will you not answer me? They said: What should we say, O Messenger of God? He said: Do you not say, ‘Did not your people expel you, and we gave you shelter? Did they not deny you, and we believed you? Did they not forsake you, and we aided you?’ He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept saying this until they knelt on their knees and said, Our wealth is in our hands for God and His Messenger. He said: Then the verse was revealed: Say, ‘I do not ask of you for this any reward but love for my relatives.’ This is how it was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn on the authority of Abd al-Mu’min ibn Ali, on the authority of Abd al-Salam, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, and it is weak in its chain of transmission, similar to it or close to it. In the two Sahihs, in the section on the spoils of Hunayn, it is close to this context, but there is no mention of the revelation of this verse. The mention of its revelation in Madinah is questionable, because the surah was revealed in Makkah, and there is no apparent connection between this verse and this context. And God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, a man named him told us, Hussein Al-Ashqar told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed, Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives,’ they said: O Messenger of God, who are these people whom God has commanded us to love? He said: Fatima and her son, may God be pleased with them both. This is a weak chain of transmission, containing an unknown person who is not known from a corrupted Shiite sheikh, namely Husayn al-Ashqar, and his report is not acceptable in this regard. It is far-fetched to mention that the verse was revealed in Medina, as it was revealed in Mecca, and Fatima, may God be pleased with her, had no children at all at that time, as she did not marry Ali, may God be pleased with him, until after Badr in the second year of the Hijra. The correct interpretation of this verse is as the scholar of the nation and interpreter of the Qur’an, Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, interpreted it, as narrated by al-Bukhari. We do not deny the recommendation regarding the people of the house and the command to be kind to them, respect them, and honor them, as they are from the pure progeny of the most honorable house on the face of the earth in pride, lineage, and lineage, especially if they follow the clear and obvious correct prophetic Sunnah, as their predecessors did, such as Abbas and his sons, Ali, and his progeny, may God be pleased with them all. It has been proven in Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon at Ghadir Khumm: “I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of God and my family. They will not separate until they return to me at the Cistern.” Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, may God be pleased with him, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, when the Quraysh meet each other, they meet them with pleasant smiles, but when they meet us, they meet us with faces we do not recognize. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became extremely angry and said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, faith will not enter a man’s heart until he loves you for the sake of God and His Messenger. Then Ahmad said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib bin Rabi’ah, who said: Al-Abbas, may God be pleased with him, entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We go out and see the Quraysh talking, but when they see us they become silent. The Messenger of God became angry and sweat trickled down between his eyes. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, faith will not enter the heart of a Muslim until he loves you for the sake of God and for my kinship. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Abdul Wahhab narrated to us, Khalid narrated to us, Shu’bah narrated to us on the authority of Waqid, who said: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of Abu Bakr - he is Al-Siddiq - may God be pleased with him, who said: “Observe Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his family.” In the Sahih, it is narrated that Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said to Ali may God be pleased with him: “By God, the kinship of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) is dearer to me than my own kinship.” And Umar ibn al-Khattab said to al-Abbas may God be pleased with them both: “By God, your conversion to Islam on the day you converted was dearer to me than the conversion of al-Khattab had he converted to Islam, because your conversion to Islam was dearer to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) than the conversion of al-Khattab.” The state of the two shaykhs may God be pleased with them is what everyone must be like, and for this reason they were the best of the believers after the prophets and messengers may God be pleased with them and with all the other companions. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Ismail bin Ibrahim narrated to us on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, who said: Yazid bin Hayyan narrated to me: I, Husayn bin Maysarah, and Umar bin Muslim went to Zayd bin Arqam, may God be pleased with him. When we sat with him, Husayn said: O Zayd, I have experienced much good. I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I heard his hadith, and I fought with him and prayed with him. O Zayd, I have seen much good. Tell us, O Zayd, what you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: O my nephew, I have grown old and my time has passed and I have forgotten some of what I remembered from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Whatever I have narrated to you, accept it, and whatever I have not narrated to you, do not burden me with it. Then he, may God be pleased with him, said: One day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to deliver a sermon to us at a watering place called Khumm between Mecca and Medina. He praised God Almighty and extolled Him, and mentioned and exhorted. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for what follows, O people, I am only a human being. It is likely that the Messenger of my Lord will come to me and I will respond. I am leaving among you two weighty things, the first of which is the Book of God Almighty in which is guidance.” And the light, so take the Book of God and hold fast to it.” So he urged and encouraged the Book of God and said, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: And the people of my household, I remind you of the people of my household, I remind you of God of the people of my household. Husayn said to him: Who are the people of his household, Zayd? Aren’t his women from the people of his household? He said: His women are not from the people of his household, but the people of his household are those for whom charity is forbidden after him. He said: Who are they? He said: They are the family of Ali, the family of Aqeel, the family of Ja’far, and the family of Abbas, may God be pleased with them. He said: Are all of these forbidden to receive charity? He said: Yes. And this is how Muslim and al-Nasa’i narrated it from the paths of Yazid ibn Hayyan. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Ali bin Al-Mundhir Al-Kufi told us, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed and Al-A’mash, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am leaving among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after me: one of them is greater than the other: the Book of God, a rope extended from the heavens to the earth, and the other is the descendants of my household, and they will not separate until they return to me at the Cistern, so see how you deal with them after me.” He is the only one who narrated it, then he said: This is a good and rare hadith. Al-Tirmidhi also said: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Kufi told us, Zaid bin Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Muhammad bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his pilgrimage on the Day of Arafah, and he was on his she-camel Al-Qaswa’, delivering a sermon. I heard him say: “O people, I have left among you that which if you adhere to, you will never go astray: the Book of God and my family, the people of my house.” Al-Tirmidhi also transmitted it alone, and he said: It is good and rare. There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Abu Dharr, Abu Saeed, Zaid bin Arqam, and Hudhayfah bin Asid, may God be pleased with them. Then Al-Tirmidhi also said: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Al-Ash'ath told us, Yahya ibn Ma'in told us, Hisham ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sulayman Al-Nawfali, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Love God Almighty for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, and love me for the love of God, and love my family for my love. Then he said: It is good and rare. We only know it from this source, and we have cited other hadiths regarding the words of God Almighty: God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification, so there is no need to repeat them here, and praise and thanks be to God. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Suwaid bin Saeed told us, Mufaddal bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hanash, who said: I heard Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, while he was holding the ring of the door, saying: O people, whoever knows me, knows me, and whoever denies me, then I am Abu Dharr. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The example of my family among you is like the example of Noah’s ship, peace be upon him. Whoever enters it will be saved, and whoever stays behind will perish.” This chain of transmission is weak. And the Almighty said: And whoever does a good deed - We will increase for him good therein. That is, whoever does a good deed - We will increase for him good therein, that is, a reward and recompense, like the Almighty’s saying: “Indeed, God does not wrong by as much as an atom’s weight. And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.” Some of the early Muslims said: Among the rewards for a good deed is another good deed after it, and among the recompenses for a bad deed is another bad deed after it. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Appreciative. That is, He forgives many bad deeds and multiplies the few good deeds, so He covers, forgives, and multiplies, so He is grateful. And the Almighty’s saying: Or do they say, ‘He has invented a lie against God?’ If God wills, He will set a seal upon your heart. That is, if you were to invent a lie against Him, as these ignorant people claim, He will set a seal upon your heart. That is, He will imprint a seal upon your heart and take away from you what He gave you of the Qur’an, like the Almighty’s saying: “And if he had invented about Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta. Then there is not one of you who could have prevented Him from it.” That is, We would not have taken the most severe vengeance against him, and no one among the people would have been able to prevent Him from it. And His statement, may He be glorified: And God will blot out falsehood is not conjoined with His statement, He seals, so it would be in the jussive mood, but rather it is in the nominative case as a subject. Ibn Jarir said: The waw was deleted from its writing in the Imam's Mushaf, just as it was deleted in His statement, We will call upon the guards and His statement, And man invokes evil as he invokes good. And His statement, the Exalted, And He will establish the truth with His words is conjoined with And God will blot out falsehood and establish the truth, meaning He will establish it, confirm it, clarify it and explain it with His words, that is, with His arguments and proofs. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts, that is, what the consciences conceal and what the secrets conceal.
42:24: God the Almighty says when He mentioned the gardens of Paradise, for His servants who believed and did righteous deeds, That is what God gives good tidings to His servants who believed and did righteous deeds. That is, this will inevitably happen to them through God’s good tidings to them. And His Almighty saying, Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.’ That is, say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists from the disbelievers of Quraysh, “I do not ask of you for this message and advice what you will not give me. Rather, I ask of you to refrain from your evil toward me and leave me to deliver the messages of my Lord. If you do not support me, then do not harm me because of the kinship between me and you.” Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Abd al-Malik ibn Maisarah, who said: I heard Tawus narrating on the authority of Ibn `Abbas may God be pleased with them both that he was asked about the verse, Except for the affection of kinship. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: The kinship of the family of Muhammad. Ibn `Abbas said: “You are hasty. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did not have a clan of Quraysh except that he had kinship with them.” He said: Except that you do not maintain kinship ties between me and you. Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it, and Imam Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Qattan narrated it on the authority of Shu`bah. `Amir al-Sha`bi, al-Dahhak, `Ali ibn Abi Talhah, al-`Awfi, Yusuf ibn Mihran, and others narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn `Abbas may God be pleased with them both. Mujahid, `Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Abu Malik, `Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others said the same. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim bin al-Qasim bin Zaid al-Tabarani and Ja’far al-Qalanisi told us: Adam bin Abi Iyas told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I do not ask of you any reward for it except that you love me for my sake because of my kinship to you and that you preserve the kinship that is between me and you. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Hasan bin Musa, Qaz’ah, meaning Ibn Suwayd bin Abi Hatim, told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muslim bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Qaz’ah bin Suwayd, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not ask of you any reward for what I have given you of clear proofs and guidance except that you love God and draw near to Him by obeying Him. Qatadah narrated something similar on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri. This is as if it is an explanation of a second statement, as if he is saying, except for love for kinship, meaning, that you do the acts of obedience that will bring you nearer to God. A third statement is what Al-Bukhari and others narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, meaning that he said: The meaning of this is that you should treat me kindly among your relatives, meaning that you should be good to them and be righteous towards them. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Al-Daylam who said: When Ali bin Al-Hussein may God be pleased with him was brought as a prisoner and was placed on the steps of Damascus, a man from the people of Ash-Sham stood up and said: Praise be to God who killed you, uprooted you, and cut off the horn of sedition. Ali bin Al-Hussein may God be pleased with him said to him: Have you recited the Qur’an? He said: Yes. He said: Have you recited Al-Ha Meem? He said: I recited the Qur’an but I did not recite Al-Ha Meem. He said: “What did you recite: ‘Say, “I do not ask of you any reward for this but the love of my relatives.”’ He said: And you are they? He said: Yes. Abu Ishaq Al-Subaie said: “I asked Amr bin Shuaib about the words of God the Most High: ‘Say, “I do not ask of you any reward for this but the love of my relatives.”’ He said: “The relatives of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him).” Both were narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Malik bin Ismail told us, Abd al-Salam told us, Yazid bin Abi Ziyad told me, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Ansar said: We did this and that, and it was as if they were boasting. Then Ibn Abbas or al-Abbas, may God be pleased with them both - Abd al-Salam was unsure - said: We have the advantage over you. report of that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he came to them in their gatherings and said: O group of Ansar, were you not humble and then God honored you through me? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Were you not astray and then God guided you through me? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Will you not answer me? They said: What should we say, O Messenger of God? He said: Do you not say, ‘Did not your people expel you, and we gave you shelter? Did they not deny you, and we believed you? Did they not forsake you, and we aided you?’ He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept saying this until they knelt on their knees and said, Our wealth is in our hands for God and His Messenger. He said: Then the verse was revealed: Say, ‘I do not ask of you for this any reward but love for my relatives.’ This is how it was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn on the authority of Abd al-Mu’min ibn Ali, on the authority of Abd al-Salam, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, and it is weak in its chain of transmission, similar to it or close to it. In the two Sahihs, in the section on the spoils of Hunayn, it is close to this context, but there is no mention of the revelation of this verse. The mention of its revelation in Madinah is questionable, because the surah was revealed in Makkah, and there is no apparent connection between this verse and this context. And God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, a man named him told us, Hussein Al-Ashqar told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed, Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives,’ they said: O Messenger of God, who are these people whom God has commanded us to love? He said: Fatima and her son, may God be pleased with them both. This is a weak chain of transmission, containing an unknown person who is not known from a corrupted Shiite sheikh, namely Husayn al-Ashqar, and his report is not acceptable in this regard. It is far-fetched to mention that the verse was revealed in Medina, as it was revealed in Mecca, and Fatima, may God be pleased with her, had no children at all at that time, as she did not marry Ali, may God be pleased with him, until after Badr in the second year of the Hijra. The correct interpretation of this verse is as the scholar of the nation and interpreter of the Qur’an, Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, interpreted it, as narrated by al-Bukhari. We do not deny the recommendation regarding the people of the house and the command to be kind to them, respect them, and honor them, as they are from the pure progeny of the most honorable house on the face of the earth in pride, lineage, and lineage, especially if they follow the clear and obvious correct prophetic Sunnah, as their predecessors did, such as Abbas and his sons, Ali, and his progeny, may God be pleased with them all. It has been proven in Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon at Ghadir Khumm: “I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of God and my family. They will not separate until they return to me at the Cistern.” Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, may God be pleased with him, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, when the Quraysh meet each other, they meet them with pleasant smiles, but when they meet us, they meet us with faces we do not recognize. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became extremely angry and said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, faith will not enter a man’s heart until he loves you for the sake of God and His Messenger. Then Ahmad said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib bin Rabi’ah, who said: Al-Abbas, may God be pleased with him, entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We go out and see the Quraysh talking, but when they see us they become silent. The Messenger of God became angry and sweat trickled down between his eyes. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, faith will not enter the heart of a Muslim until he loves you for the sake of God and for my kinship. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Abdul Wahhab narrated to us, Khalid narrated to us, Shu’bah narrated to us on the authority of Waqid, who said: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of Abu Bakr - he is Al-Siddiq - may God be pleased with him, who said: “Observe Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his family.” In the Sahih, it is narrated that Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said to Ali may God be pleased with him: “By God, the kinship of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) is dearer to me than my own kinship.” And Umar ibn al-Khattab said to al-Abbas may God be pleased with them both: “By God, your conversion to Islam on the day you converted was dearer to me than the conversion of al-Khattab had he converted to Islam, because your conversion to Islam was dearer to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) than the conversion of al-Khattab.” The state of the two shaykhs may God be pleased with them is what everyone must be like, and for this reason they were the best of the believers after the prophets and messengers may God be pleased with them and with all the other companions. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Ismail bin Ibrahim narrated to us on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, who said: Yazid bin Hayyan narrated to me: I, Husayn bin Maysarah, and Umar bin Muslim went to Zayd bin Arqam, may God be pleased with him. When we sat with him, Husayn said: O Zayd, I have experienced much good. I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I heard his hadith, and I fought with him and prayed with him. O Zayd, I have seen much good. Tell us, O Zayd, what you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: O my nephew, I have grown old and my time has passed and I have forgotten some of what I remembered from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Whatever I have narrated to you, accept it, and whatever I have not narrated to you, do not burden me with it. Then he, may God be pleased with him, said: One day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to deliver a sermon to us at a watering place called Khumm between Mecca and Medina. He praised God Almighty and extolled Him, and mentioned and exhorted. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for what follows, O people, I am only a human being. It is likely that the Messenger of my Lord will come to me and I will respond. I am leaving among you two weighty things, the first of which is the Book of God Almighty in which is guidance.” And the light, so take the Book of God and hold fast to it.” So he urged and encouraged the Book of God and said, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: And the people of my household, I remind you of the people of my household, I remind you of God of the people of my household. Husayn said to him: Who are the people of his household, Zayd? Aren’t his women from the people of his household? He said: His women are not from the people of his household, but the people of his household are those for whom charity is forbidden after him. He said: Who are they? He said: They are the family of Ali, the family of Aqeel, the family of Ja’far, and the family of Abbas, may God be pleased with them. He said: Are all of these forbidden to receive charity? He said: Yes. And this is how Muslim and al-Nasa’i narrated it from the paths of Yazid ibn Hayyan. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Ali bin Al-Mundhir Al-Kufi told us, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed and Al-A’mash, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am leaving among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after me: one of them is greater than the other: the Book of God, a rope extended from the heavens to the earth, and the other is the descendants of my household, and they will not separate until they return to me at the Cistern, so see how you deal with them after me.” He is the only one who narrated it, then he said: This is a good and rare hadith. Al-Tirmidhi also said: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Kufi told us, Zaid bin Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Muhammad bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his pilgrimage on the Day of Arafah, and he was on his she-camel Al-Qaswa’, delivering a sermon. I heard him say: “O people, I have left among you that which if you adhere to, you will never go astray: the Book of God and my family, the people of my house.” Al-Tirmidhi also transmitted it alone, and he said: It is good and rare. There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Abu Dharr, Abu Saeed, Zaid bin Arqam, and Hudhayfah bin Asid, may God be pleased with them. Then Al-Tirmidhi also said: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Al-Ash'ath told us, Yahya ibn Ma'in told us, Hisham ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sulayman Al-Nawfali, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Love God Almighty for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, and love me for the love of God, and love my family for my love. Then he said: It is good and rare. We only know it from this source, and we have cited other hadiths regarding the words of God Almighty: God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification, so there is no need to repeat them here, and praise and thanks be to God. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Suwaid bin Saeed told us, Mufaddal bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hanash, who said: I heard Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, while he was holding the ring of the door, saying: O people, whoever knows me, knows me, and whoever denies me, then I am Abu Dharr. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The example of my family among you is like the example of Noah’s ship, peace be upon him. Whoever enters it will be saved, and whoever stays behind will perish.” This chain of transmission is weak. And the Almighty said: And whoever does a good deed - We will increase for him good therein. That is, whoever does a good deed - We will increase for him good therein, that is, a reward and recompense, like the Almighty’s saying: “Indeed, God does not wrong by as much as an atom’s weight. And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.” Some of the early Muslims said: Among the rewards for a good deed is another good deed after it, and among the recompenses for a bad deed is another bad deed after it. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Appreciative. That is, He forgives many bad deeds and multiplies the few good deeds, so He covers, forgives, and multiplies, so He is grateful. And the Almighty’s saying: Or do they say, ‘He has invented a lie against God?’ If God wills, He will set a seal upon your heart. That is, if you were to invent a lie against Him, as these ignorant people claim, He will set a seal upon your heart. That is, He will imprint a seal upon your heart and take away from you what He gave you of the Qur’an, like the Almighty’s saying: “And if he had invented about Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta. Then there is not one of you who could have prevented Him from it.” That is, We would not have taken the most severe vengeance against him, and no one among the people would have been able to prevent Him from it. And His statement, may He be glorified: And God will blot out falsehood is not conjoined with His statement, He seals, so it would be in the jussive mood, but rather it is in the nominative case as a subject. Ibn Jarir said: The waw was deleted from its writing in the Imam's Mushaf, just as it was deleted in His statement, We will call upon the guards and His statement, And man invokes evil as he invokes good. And His statement, the Exalted, And He will establish the truth with His words is conjoined with And God will blot out falsehood and establish the truth, meaning He will establish it, confirm it, clarify it and explain it with His words, that is, with His arguments and proofs. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts, that is, what the consciences conceal and what the secrets conceal.
42:25: God Almighty says, thanking His servants for accepting their repentance to Him if they repent and return to Him, that it is from His generosity and forbearance that He pardons, overlooks, conceals, and forgives, as He Almighty says: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. It has been proven in Sahih Muslim, may God have mercy on him, where he said: Muhammad bin Al-Sabah and Zuhair bin Harb told us: Omar bin Yunus told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Ishaq bin Abi Talhah told us, Anas bin Malik told me, and he is his uncle, may God be pleased with him. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God is more pleased with the repentance of His servant when he repents to Him than one of you whose mount was in a desert and it slipped away from him with his food and drink on it. He despaired of finding it, so he went to a tree and lay down in its shade, having despaired of finding his mount. While he was like that, suddenly it was standing next to him. He took hold of its reins and said, out of intense joy: ‘O God, You are my servant and I am your Lord.’ He made a mistake out of intense joy.” It has also been proven in Sahih from the narration of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, something similar. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, regarding the verse: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants, that Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: God rejoices more over the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his lost animal in a place where he fears that thirst may kill him. Hammam bin Al-Harith said: Ibn Masoud may God be pleased with him was asked about a man who commits adultery with a woman and then marries her. He said: There is nothing wrong with it. Then he recited: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants, the verse. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Shuraih Al-Qadi on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i on the authority of Hammam, and he mentioned it. The verse: And pardons misdeeds, meaning He accepts repentance in the future and pardons misdeeds in the past. And He knows what you do, meaning He knows everything you have done, made, and said, and despite this He accepts the repentance of whoever repents to Him. And the Almighty’s saying: And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds. Al-Suddi said: He means He responds to them. Ibn Jarir said the same: Its meaning is He responds to their supplications for themselves, their companions and their brothers. He narrated it from some grammarians, and that he made it like the Almighty’s saying: And their Lord responded to them. Then he and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Al-A’mash from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Salamah ibn Sabra, who said: Muadh, may God be pleased with him, delivered a sermon to us in Syria, and he said: You are the believers and you are the people of Paradise. By God, I hope that God Almighty will admit those whom you curse from among the Persians and Romans into Paradise, and that is because if one of you does a deed for Him - meaning one of them - he says: You have done well, may God have mercy on you, you have done well, may God bless you. Then he recited: And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of some of the Arab scholars that he made his statement, Those who listen to the word, meaning those who respond to the truth and follow it, like the statement of God, the Most High, Only those who listen respond, and God will raise the dead. The first meaning is more evident for His statement, and will increase them from His bounty, meaning He will answer their supplications beyond that. For this reason, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us, Baqiyyah told us, Ismail ibn Abdullah al-Kindi told us, al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding His statement, the Most High, and will increase them from His bounty, that he said, Intercession is for those who are entitled to Hellfire, from among those who did them good in this world. Qatadah said on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i al-Lakhmi regarding His statement, the Most High, and will increase them from His bounty, that he said, They will intercede for their brothers. And the Almighty said, And for the disbelievers is a severe punishment. When He mentioned the believers and their great reward, He mentioned the disbelievers and their severe, painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection, the day of their return and reckoning. God Almighty says: And if God were to expand the provision for His servants, they would transgress upon the earth. That is, if He were to give them more provision than they needed, it would lead them to transgress and tyranny, some of them against others, out of evil and arrogance. Qatada said: It was said that the best life is that which does not distract you nor make you arrogant. Qatada mentioned, I only fear for you what God Almighty brings forth from the splendor of worldly life. The questioner’s question is: Does good bring evil? The hadith. And the Almighty’s saying: “But He sends down in due measure as He wills. Indeed, He is aware of His servants and seeing them.” That is, but He provides them with provision that He chooses from what is best for them, and He knows best about that. He enriches those who deserve to be rich and impoverishes those who deserve to be poor, as came in the narrated hadith: “Among My servants is he who is not righteous except by wealth, and if I were to impoverish him, I would corrupt his religion. And among My servants is he who is not righteous except by poverty, and if I were to make him rich, I would corrupt his religion.” God the Almighty says: {And it is He who sends down rain after they have despaired} meaning, after people have given up hope of rain, He sends it down upon them at a time of their need and poverty, as God the Almighty says: {And although they were, before it sent down upon them, in despair}. And God the Almighty says: {And spreads His mercy} meaning, He makes it widespread among the people of that region and that area. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that a man said to Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him: O Commander of the Faithful, the rain has dried up and the people have despaired. Umar may God be pleased with him said: You have been given rain, then he recited: {And it is He who sends down rain after they have despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy} meaning, He is the One who disposes of His creation in a way that benefits them in this world and the hereafter, and He is the One whose outcome is praiseworthy in all that He decrees and does.
