Some of them said to him: We are saddened by what we see in you. He said: Do not be sad about what you see, for what you see is due to a sin, and what God pardons is more. Then he recited this verse: {And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much.} My father told us, Yahya bin Al-Hamid Al-Hammani told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abi Al-Bilad, who said: I said to Al-Ala bin Badr, Whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned, and I lost my sight when I was a boy. He said, Then it is for the sins of your parents. My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad Al-Tanafisi told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Abdul-Aziz bin Abi Dawud, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: We do not know of anyone who memorized the Qur’an and then forgot it except for a sin. Then Ad-Dahhak recited, “Whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much,” and Ad-Dahhak said: What disaster is greater than forgetting the Qur’an? Ibn Abbas said: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake meaning it moves from beneath it and the earth discharges its burdens meaning it throws out the dead that are in it. This was said by more than one of the early Muslims. This is like the words of God Almighty: “O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing” and His words: And when the earth is extended * And casts out what is in it and becomes empty. Muslim said in his Sahih: Wasil ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The earth casts out the most precious pieces of its liver like columns of gold and silver. Then the murderer will come and say, ‘For this I killed,’ and the severer will come and say, ‘For this I severed my ties of kinship,’ and the thief will come and say, ‘For this I cut off my hand.’ Then they will leave him and take nothing from him.” And God Almighty said: And man will say, ‘What is [wrong] with her?’ meaning he will be astonished by her situation after she had been stable and motionless, and he was settled on her back, meaning the situation changed. Then it became agitated and disturbed, and the command of God Almighty came to it, which He had prepared for it, of an earthquake from which it could not escape. Then it cast out what was in its womb of the dead, of the first and the last. Then the people were astonished by its action, and the earth was changed into another earth, and the heavens, and they appeared before God, the One, the Compeller. God the Almighty said: {On that Day it will declare its report} meaning it will declare what those who worked on its back did. Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us. At-Tirmidhi and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa’i said - and the wording is his - Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, Abdullah - he is Ibn al-Mubarak - from Sa’id ibn Abi Ayyub - from Yahya ibn Abi Sulayman - from Sa’id al-Maqburi - from Abu Hurayrah who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this verse: {On that Day it will declare its report}. He said: Do you know what its report is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Its report is that it will testify against every male and female slave regarding what they did on its back, that it will say, ‘He did such and such on such and such a day.’ This is its report.” Then At-Tirmidhi said: This is a sahih gharib hadith. In Mu’jam At-Tabarani, from the hadith of Ibn Lahi’ah, Al-Harith ibn Yazid told me that he heard Rabia Al-Hadsi say: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Beware of the earth, for it is your mother, and there is no one who works on it, good or evil, except that it will inform you.” God the Almighty said: {That your Lord has inspired to her} Al-Bukhari said: He inspired to her, He inspired to her, He inspired to her, and He revealed to her are one thing. Ibn Abbas said the same: He inspired to her, meaning He inspired to her. It appears that this is implied with the meaning of He gave her permission. Shabib bin Bishr said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: {On that Day she will tell her report} He said: Her Lord will say to her, and she said. Mujahid said: He inspired to her, meaning He commanded her. Al-Qurazi said: He commanded her to split apart from them. God the Almighty said: {On that Day mankind will proceed in separate groups} That is, they will return from the place of reckoning in separate groups, meaning in various types and kinds, between the wretched and the happy, some commanded to go to Paradise and some commanded to go to Hell. Ibn Jurayj said: They will be split apart in separate groups and will not come together at the end of what is upon them. Al-Suddi said: In separate groups. God Almighty says: So that they may see their deeds, meaning that they may know what they did in this world of good and evil. This is why He says: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. Al-Bukhari said: Ismail bin Abdullah told us, Malik told me, from Zaid bin Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Horses are for three: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a cover, and for a man they are a burden. As for the one who has a reward, it is a man who ties them up in the cause of God and lets them run long in a meadow or a garden, and whatever they do in that meadow or garden is a good deed for him. If they cut their ties and reach a hill or two, their tracks and dung are good deeds for him. If they pass by a river and drink from it, and he does not intend to be watered by it, that is a good deed for him, and they are a reward for that man. A man ties them up out of self-sufficiency and chastity, and does not forget God’s right over their necks and backs, they are a cover for him. A man ties them up for pride, showing off, and to please others, and they are a burden for that man. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about donkeys, and he said: “God did not reveal anything about them except this unique and comprehensive verse: ‘So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it. ’” *And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.” Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, Jarir bin Hazim narrated to us, Al-Hasan narrated to us, on the authority of Sa’sa’ah bin Mu’awiyah, the uncle of Al-Farazdaq, “That he came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and recited to him: ‘So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.’ He said: It is enough for me; I do not care that I do not hear anything else.’” This is how An-Nasa’i narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Yunus Al-Mu’addib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said: Sa’sa’ah, the uncle of Al-Farazdaq, narrated to us, and he mentioned it. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Adi, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Protect yourselves from the Fire, even if it is with half a date or with a kind word. And he also has in Sahih: Do not despise any good deed, even if it is emptying your bucket into the vessel of the one who is asking for water, or meeting your brother with a cheerful face. And in Sahih also: O believing women, do not despise a neighbor’s kindness to her neighbor, even if it is a sheep’s hoof, meaning its hoof. And in another hadith: Return the beggar even if it is with a burnt hoof. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Ansari told us, Kathir ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of al-Muttalib ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Aisha, protect yourself from the Fire, even with half a date, for it will satisfy the hunger of the one who is full. Ahmad alone narrated it. It was narrated that Aisha gave away a grape in charity and said: How many atoms’ weight is in it? Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir told us, Sa’id ibn Muslim told us, I heard Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Awf ibn al-Harith ibn al-Tufayl told me, that Aisha told him that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: O Aisha, beware of small sins, for God will seek them. An-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sa’id ibn Muslim ibn Banu Ka’b. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Al-Khattab Al-Hassani told me, Al-Haytham bin Al-Rabi’ told us, Samak bin Atiyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abi Qilabah, on the authority of Anas, who said: “Abu Bakr was eating with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when this verse was revealed: ‘So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.’ Abu Bakr raised his hand and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I will be rewarded for what I have done, even an atom’s weight of evil.’ He said: ‘O Abu Bakr, whatever you have seen in this world that you dislike is for the weight of an atom of evil, and God will store up for you the weight of an atom of good until you die on the Day of Resurrection.’” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abi Al-Khattab, and then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, ‘Abd Al-Wahhab told us, Ayoub told us, he said: In the book of Abi Qilabah, on the authority of Abi Idris, that Abu Bakr was eating with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it. He also narrated it on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Qilabah, that Abu Bakr and he mentioned it. Another path Ibn Jarir said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Yahya bin Abdullah told me on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Habli on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-As that he said when the verse When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake was revealed and Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, was sitting, he cried when it was revealed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What makes you cry, O Abu Bakr? He said: This surah makes me cry. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Were it not that you make mistakes and sin, and God forgives you, God would have created a nation that would make mistakes and sin, and He would forgive them. Another Hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah and Ali ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughira, known as Bil’an al-Misri, told us: Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told us: Hisham ibn Sa’d told me, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: When the verse, So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it, was revealed, I said, O Messenger of God, will I see my deeds? He said, Yes. I said, Those are the great, the great. He said, Yes. I said, The small, the small? He said, Yes. I said, May my mother be bereaved! He said, “Be of good cheer, O Abu Sa’id, for a good deed is rewarded tenfold—meaning up to seven hundred times—and God multiplies for whomever He wills, and a bad deed is rewarded likewise, or God pardons. And none of you will be saved by his deeds.” I said, Not even you, O Messenger of God? He said, Not even me, unless God covers me with mercy from Him. Abu Zur’ah said: This was not narrated by anyone other than Ibn Lahi’ah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Yahya bin Abdullah bin Bakir told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, Ata’ bin Dinar told me, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, regarding the statement of God, the Most High: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. That was when this verse was revealed: And they give food, in spite of love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive. The Muslims used to think that they would not be rewarded for a small amount if they gave it. A needy person would come to their door, and they would think it was insignificant to give him a date, a piece of bread, a walnut, or something similar, but they would reject it and say: This is nothing. We are only rewarded for what we give and we love it. Others used to think that they would not be blamed for a small sin: a lie, a glance, backbiting, and the like. They say: God promised Hell for major sins, so He encouraged them to do a little good, because it is likely to increase, and He warned them against a little evil, because it is likely to increase. So the verse was revealed: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it meaning the weight of the smallest ant, in his book and it will make him happy. He said: For every righteous and wicked person, one bad deed will be recorded for every bad deed, and for every good deed, ten good deeds will be recorded. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, God will multiply the good deeds of the believers also by ten for every one, and will erase ten bad deeds for every good deed. So if his good deeds exceed his bad deeds by an atom’s weight, he will enter Paradise. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, Imran told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abd Rabbih, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of small sins, for they accumulate in a man until they destroy him.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, gave an example of them, like a people who settled in a desert land and witnessed the actions of the people. One man would go and bring a stick, and another would bring a stick, until they had gathered a great number of people, lit a fire, and cooked what they had thrown into it. The end of the interpretation of Surat Al-Zalzalah. Praise and thanks be to God.
42:31: God Almighty says: And among His signs which indicate His greatness, tremendous power and overwhelming authority is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed throughout them meaning He has scattered throughout them in the heavens and the earth of living creatures This includes the angels, mankind, the jinn and all other animals with their different shapes, colors, languages, natures, kinds and types. He has dispersed them throughout the regions of the heavens and the earth. And He with all of this is able to gather them together if He wills meaning on the Day of Resurrection He will gather the first and the last and all other creatures on one plain where the caller will hear them and their sight will penetrate them, and He will judge them with His just and true judgment. And the Almighty said: And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned meaning, whatever disasters befall you, O people, it is only because of sins that have gone before you. But He pardons much meaning, of the sins, so He does not punish you for them, rather He pardons them. And if God were to punish people for what they have earned, He would not leave a creature on the earth’s surface. And in the authentic hadith: “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, no fatigue, illness, anxiety, or grief befalls a believer except that God expiates for him some of his sins because of it, even the prick he receives from a thorn.” Ibn Jarir said: Ya`qub ibn Ibrahim told us, Ibn `Ulayyah told us, Ayyub told us: I read in the book of Abu Qilabah that the verse, So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it was revealed while Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him was eating. He stopped and said: O Messenger of God, I see what I have done of good and evil. He said: What you have seen that you dislike is from the weight of an atom of evil, and the weight of good is saved up until it is given to you on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Abu Idris said: I see its proof in the Book of God the Most High: “And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much.” Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Qilabah on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him. He said: The first is more correct. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Isa ibn al-Tabba’ told us, Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah al-Fazari told us, al-Azhar ibn Rashid al-Kahili told us, on the authority of al-Khidr ibn al-Qawwas al-Bajali, on the authority of Abu Sakhila, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Shall I not tell you of the best verse in the Book of God Almighty, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us about it? He said: “Whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much.” And I will explain it to you, Ali: Whatever strikes you of illness, punishment, or affliction in this world - it is for what your hands have earned. And God is too forbearing to repeat the punishment in the Hereafter. And whatever God pardons in this world - God is too generous to return after His pardon. Imam Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah and Abdah, on the authority of Abu Sakhila, who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said, and he mentioned something similar with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from another chain of transmission, without a chain of transmission ending with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: My father told us, Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim told us, Abu Saeed ibn Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Juhaifa, who said: I entered upon Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and he said: Shall I not tell you a hadith that every believer should remember? So we asked him, and he recited this verse: “And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much.” He said: Whatever God punishes in this world, God is too forbearing to praise it with punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And whatever God pardons in this world, God is too generous to repeat His pardon on the Day of Resurrection. Imam Ahmad said: Ya`la ibn `Ubayd told us, Talha, meaning Ibn Yahya, told us, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Mu`awiyah, who is Ibn Abi Sufyan, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is nothing that befalls a believer in his body that harms him, except that God Almighty expiates some of his sins because of it. Imam Ahmad also said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Za`idah, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of `Aishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the sins of a servant increase and he does not have anything with which to expiate them, God Almighty will afflict him with sadness in order to expiate them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Muslim, on the authority of al-Hasan, who is al-Basri, who said about the words of God, the Most High: {And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much.} He said: When this was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, there is no scratch of a stick, no twitching of a vein, and no stumble except for a sin. But what God pardons is more.} He also said: My father told us, Umar ibn Ali told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, may God be pleased with him, who said: Some of his companions came to him and he had been afflicted with a physical ailment. Some of them said to him: We are saddened by what we see in you. He said: Do not be sad about what you see, for what you see is due to a sin, and what God pardons is more. Then he recited this verse: {And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much.} My father told us, Yahya bin Al-Hamid Al-Hammani told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abi Al-Bilad, who said: I said to Al-Ala bin Badr, Whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned, and I lost my sight when I was a boy. He said, Then it is for the sins of your parents. My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad Al-Tanafisi told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Abdul-Aziz bin Abi Dawud, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: We do not know of anyone who memorized the Qur’an and then forgot it except for a sin. Then Ad-Dahhak recited, “Whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much,” and Ad-Dahhak said: What disaster is greater than forgetting the Qur’an?
42:32: God Almighty says: And among His signs that indicate His dazzling power and authority is His subjecting the sea so that ships may sail through it by His command. These are the ships in the sea like flags, that is, like mountains. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Al-Suddi, and Al-Dahhak said: That is, these in the sea are like mountains on land. If He wills, He can still the wind, that is, the wind that moves the ships in the sea. If He willed, He could still it so that it would not move the ships, but would remain still, neither coming nor going, but standing on its back, that is, on the surface of the water. Indeed in that are signs for everyone who is patient, that is, in times of hardship, grateful. That is, in His subjecting the sea and causing it to run as much as they need for their navigation, there are indications of His blessings upon His creation for everyone who is patient, that is, in times of hardship, grateful, in times of ease. And the Almighty’s saying, Or destroy them for what they have earned, meaning, if He had willed, He could have destroyed the ships and sunk them for the sins of their people who were riding in them. And pardon many, meaning of their sins. And if He had taken them to task for all their sins, He would have destroyed everyone who traveled the sea. Some scholars of interpretation said that the meaning of the Almighty’s statement, Or destroy them for what they have earned, is that if He willed, He could have sent a strong, violent wind that would have taken the ships and diverted them from their straight course, turning them to the right or to the left, running away, not traveling on a path or in a direction they intended. This statement includes their destruction, and it is appropriate for the first, which is that if He willed, He could have made the wind stop and they would have stopped, or He could have made it strong and they would have been scattered, run away and perished. However, from His kindness and mercy, He sends it according to need, just as He sends rain in sufficient quantities, and if He sent down a very large amount, it would have demolished buildings, or a small amount, it would not have produced crops and fruits, to the point that He sends to a land like Egypt a flood from another land, because they do not need rain, and if He sent it down upon them, it would have demolished their buildings and brought down their walls. The Almighty said, And those who dispute concerning Our verses know that there is no escape for them, meaning there is no escape for them from Our punishment and vengeance, for they are overcome by Our power.

The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was doing something with his hand but did not notice her, so I moved his hand until I made him notice her and he stopped. Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud’an often mentions objectionable things in his narrations, and this is objectionable. Then I saw the face of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) beaming.” This is the wording of al-Nasa’i. Al-Bazzar said: Yusuf bin Musa told us, Abu Ghassan told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever supplicates against the one who has wronged him has taken revenge. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abu Hamza, whose name is Maymun. Then he said: We do not know it except from his hadith, and he has spoken about it because of his memory. And the Almighty’s statement: The way means that hardship and suffering is only upon those who oppress people and transgress upon the earth without right meaning that they initiate injustice against people, as it came in the authentic hadith: The two who slander each other shall not be blamed for what they say, but upon the aggressor is he who has not retaliated. “For those is a painful punishment” meaning severe and painful. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah said: Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Saeed bin Zaid, the brother of Hammad bin Zaid, told us, Uthman Al-Shaham told us, Muhammad bin Was’ told us: I arrived in Mecca and there was a view of the Trench, so I took what I needed and he took me to Marwan bin Al-Muhallab, who was the governor of Basra. He said: What is your need, O Abu Abdullah? I said: My need is if I can be as the brother of Banu Adi was. He said: Who is the brother of Banu Adi? Al-Ala’ ibn Ziyad said: He once appointed a friend of his to a job, so he wrote to him: As for what follows, if you are able to not spend the night unless your back is light, your stomach is empty, and your hands are clean of the blood and wealth of Muslims, then if you do that, then there will be no blame upon you: “The blame is only against those who wrong people and transgress upon the earth without right. Those will have a painful punishment.” Marwan said: By God, he spoke the truth and advised. Then he said: What is your need, O Abu Abdullah? I said: My need is for you to join my family. He said: Yes. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Meaning, it is of the matters that God has commanded, meaning it is of the matters that are to be praised and the praiseworthy deeds for which there is a great reward and beautiful praise. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Imran bin Musa al-Tarsusi told us, Musmad bin Yazid, the servant of al-Fudayl bin Ayyad, told us: I heard al-Fudayl bin Ayyad say: If a man comes to you complaining about another man, say: O my brother, forgive him, for forgiveness is closer to piety. If he says: My heart cannot bear forgiveness, but I will vindicate myself as God the Almighty has commanded me, then say to him: If you are good at vindicating yourself, then fine, otherwise return to the door of forgiveness, for it is a wide door. For whoever forgives and makes peace, his reward is with God. The one who forgives sleeps in his bed at night, and the one who vindicates turns things around. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya, meaning Ibn Saeed Al-Qattan, narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, Saeed narrated to us on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “A man insulted Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to admire and smile. When he repeated the insult, he responded to some of what he said, so the Prophet became angry and stood up. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, caught up with him and said: ‘O Messenger of God, he was insulting me while you were sitting, and when you responded to some of what he said, you became angry and stood up.’ He said: ‘There was an angel with you responding on your behalf, but when you responded to some of what he said, Satan came, so I would not sit with Satan.’ Then he said: ‘O Abu Bakr, three things are all true: No servant is wronged and God overlooks it, except that God Almighty will honor him and grant him victory because of it. No man opens the door of giving, intending thereby to be kind, except that God will increase it for him in abundance. No man opens the door of asking, intending thereby to be kind, except that God Almighty will increase it for him in scarcity.’” Abu Dawud also narrated it on the authority of Abd Al-A’la Ibn Hammad on the authority of Sufyan Ibn Uyaynah. He said: Sufyan Ibn Isa narrated it. Both of them are on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, and he narrated it on the authority of Al-Layth on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi on the authority of Bashir ibn Al-Muharrir on the authority of Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, with no chain of transmission. This hadith is extremely good in meaning, and it is appropriate for Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him.

42:46: God Almighty says, informing about His noble self that whatever He wills happens and there is no one to prevent it, and whatever He does not will does not happen and there is no one to create it, and that whoever God guides cannot be led astray, and whoever God leads astray cannot be guided, as God Almighty says: And whomsoever He leads astray, you will never find for him a protector to guide him. Then God Almighty says, informing about the wrongdoers, who are the polytheists: When they see the punishment, meaning the Day of Resurrection, they will wish to return to this world, they will say, ‘Is there any way back?’ as God Almighty says: “And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, ‘Oh, would that we could be sent back and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers.’ Rather, what they concealed before will become apparent to them, and if they were sent back, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars.” God the Almighty says: And you will see them exposed to it meaning the Fire humbled by humiliation meaning that which has befallen them because of their past disobedience to God the Almighty. Looking from a hidden corner Mujahid said: meaning humiliated, meaning they look at it stealthily out of fear of it, and that which they are wary of will inevitably befall them, and what is greater than what is in their souls, may God protect us from that. And those who believe will say meaning they will say on the Day of Resurrection Indeed, the losers meaning the greatest loss are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection meaning they are taken to the Fire and lost their pleasure in the eternal home and lost themselves, and they are separated from their loved ones, companions, families and relatives, so they lose them. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers will be in an enduring punishment meaning, perpetual and everlasting, from which they will have no escape or way out. God the Almighty says: And they will have no protectors to aid them other than God meaning, to rescue them from the torment and humiliation they are in. And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no way meaning, there is no escape.
42:47: When God Almighty mentioned the horrors and terrible things that will happen on the Day of Resurrection, He warned against them and commanded people to prepare for them, saying: Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from God for which there is no repelling. That is, if He commands it to happen, it will happen in the blink of an eye, and there is no repelling or preventing it. And the Almighty said: For you there will be no refuge that Day, nor will you be any denier. That is, you will have no fortress in which to protect yourself, nor a place to conceal yourself in which to hide, so that you will be hidden from His sight, the Blessed and Exalted. Rather, He encompasses you with His knowledge, sight, and power, so there is no refuge from Him except to Him. “On that Day, man will say, ‘Where is the refuge?’ No! There is no blame. To your Lord, that Day, is the final settlement.” And the Almighty said: But if they turn away, meaning the polytheists, then We have not sent you over them as a guardian, meaning you have no control over them. And the Almighty said: It is not upon you to guide them, but God guides whom He wills. And the Almighty said: Upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the account. And the Almighty said here: Upon you is only the conveyance, meaning We have only charged you with conveying God’s message to them. Then He, the Blessed and Exalted, said: And indeed, when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it. That is, if ease and blessings befall him, he rejoices in that. But if evil befalls them, that is, the people, then indeed, man is ungrateful. That is, he denies the blessings that came before him and does not know anything except the present moment. If a blessing befalls him, he becomes wicked and arrogant, and if a trial befalls him, he despairs and loses hope, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the women: O group of women, give charity, for I have seen that you are the majority of the people of Hellfire. A woman said: Why, O Messenger of God? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Because you complain a lot and are ungrateful to your husbands. If you treat one of them well for a lifetime, then leave her one day, she will say: ‘I have never seen any good from you.’” This is the case with most women, except for those whom God Almighty guides and inspires with His right path, and who are among those who believe and do righteous deeds. The believer is as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “If something good happens to him, he is thankful and that is good for him. If something bad happens to him, he is patient and that is good for him. This is not the case for anyone except the believer.”

42:49: God the Almighty informs us that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, their Owner and Disposer of them, and that whatever He wills happens and whatever He does not will does not happen, and that He gives to whomever He wills and withholds from whomever He wills, and there is no one who can withhold what He gives nor give what He withholds, and that He creates what He wills. He gives to whomever He wills female [children] meaning He only grants him daughters. Al-Baghawi said: Among them was Lot, peace be upon him. And He gives to whomever He wills males meaning He only grants him sons. Al-Baghawi said: Like Abraham, peace be upon him, who did not have a female child. Or He pairs them [with children], male and female meaning He gives to whomever He wills among the people two mates, a male and a female, meaning this and that. Al-Baghawi said: Like Muhammad, peace be upon him. And He makes whomever He wills barren meaning he does not have children. Al-Baghawi said: “Like Yahya and Jesus, peace be upon them, so He divided people into four categories: some He gives daughters, some He gives sons, some He gives both males and females, and some He denies both, making them sterile, with no offspring or children. “He is All-Knowing” means who deserves each of these categories. Powerful means over whomever He wills, of the differences between people in that. This situation is similar to what God, the Most High, said about Jesus, peace be upon him: And We will make him a sign to the people, meaning an indication of His Almighty and Holy Power, as He created creation into four categories. Adam, peace be upon him, was created from dust, not from a male and a female. Eve, peace be upon her, was created from a male without a female. All creation except Jesus, peace be upon him, was from a male and a female, and Jesus, peace be upon him, was created from a female without a male. Thus, the indication was completed by creating Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon them. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: And We will make him a sign to the people. This situation is about fathers and the first situation is about children, and each of them has four categories. So glory be to the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.

42:51: These are the stations of revelation in relation to the Paradise of God, the Almighty, the Majestic, and that is that God, the Blessed and Exalted, sometimes casts into the mind of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, something that there is no doubt is from God, the Almighty, the Majestic, as came in Sahih Ibn Hibban on the authority of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: The Holy Spirit inspired in my mind that no soul will die until it has completed its provision and its appointed time, so fear God and be moderate in your request. And the Almighty’s saying: or from behind a veil is like what He spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, as he asked to see Him after speaking, but He was veiled from him. In the Sahih, it is reported that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both: God does not speak to anyone except from behind a veil, and He spoke to your father directly. This is what is stated in the hadith. He had been killed on the Day of Uhud, but this was in the intermediate realm, and the verse only applies to this world. And God, the Almighty, said: Or He sends a messenger to reveal by His permission whatever He wills, just as Gabriel, peace be upon him, and other angels descended upon the prophets, peace be upon them. Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Aware, All-Wise. And God, the Almighty, said: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit by Our command, meaning the Qur’an. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was, meaning, according to the details prescribed for you in the Qur’an. But We have made it, meaning the Qur’an, a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants, like His statement, the Almighty, “Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guide and a healing. But those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is, upon them, blindness.’” And the Almighty’s saying: And indeed, you meaning O Muhammad guide to a straight path which is the upright character, then He explained it with the Almighty’s saying: The path of God meaning and His law that God has commanded To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth meaning their Lord and Owner and the One who disposes of them and the Ruler whose judgment cannot be questioned Unquestionably, to God do all matters return meaning matters return and He decides and rules in them, glory be to Him, and He is far above what the wrongdoers and deniers say, far above.

God the Almighty tells us about His greatness and majesty and that He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in them and everything in between them and that He is the Most Gracious whose mercy encompasses all things. And His statement: They do not possess any speech from Him means that no one is able to initiate a speech to Him except with His permission, as in His statement: Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? And His statement: The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak. The commentators differed as to what is meant by the Spirit here. According to some sayings: One of them is what Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they are the spirits of the children of Adam. The second they are the children of Adam, as was said by Al-Hasan and Qatadah. Qatada said: This is one of the things that Ibn Abbas kept secret. Third That they are creations of God in the form of the sons of Adam and they are neither angels nor human beings, and they eat and drink. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Salih and Al-A’mash. Fourth That they are Gabriel. This was said by Al-Sha’bi, Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Al-Dahhak. Evidence for this statement is the saying of God the Almighty: The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart that you may be among the warners. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Spirit is the most noble of the angels and the closest to God the Almighty and the bearer of revelation. Fifth That they are the Qur’an. This was said by Ibn Zayd, like His saying: And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit of Our command (Al-Anfal 11:1). Sixth That they are angels equal in stature to all creatures. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said that Ibn Abbas said: Regarding his statement: The Day the Spirit will arise, he said: He is a great angel, the greatest of the angels in creation. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told us, Rawad ibn al-Jarrah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Spirit is in the fourth heaven. It is greater than the heavens, the mountains, and the angels. It glorifies God twelve thousand times every day. God creates from every glorification an angel from the angels who will come on the Day of Resurrection in a row by themselves. This is a very strange statement. At-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Aras al-Misri told us, Wahb God ibn Rawq ibn Hubayrah told us, Bishr ibn Bakr told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Ata’ told me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “God has an angel who, if he were to be told to swallow the seven heavens and the earths in one morsel, he would do so. His glorification is ‘Glory be to You wherever you are.’” This is a very strange hadith, and there is doubt about its being attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It may be attributed to Ibn Abbas, or it may be from what he received from the Israelite narratives. And God knows best. Ibn Jarir stopped and did not confirm any of these statements. What is most likely to me, and God knows best, is that they are the sons of Adam. And the saying of God the Almighty: Except for he whom the Most Gracious has permitted is like His saying: The Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission and as is proven in the Sahih: And none will speak that Day except the messengers and His saying: And he will say what is right meaning the truth and from the truth is there is no god but God as Abu Salih and Ikrimah said. And His saying: That is the true Day meaning the one that will inevitably come So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way of return meaning a return, a path to be guided to Him and a method to follow. And His saying the Almighty: Indeed, We have warned you of an imminent torment meaning the Day of Resurrection because its occurrence is certain, it has become imminent because everything that is coming is coming The Day a man will see what his hands have put forth meaning all of his deeds, the good and the bad, will be presented to him. Its ancient and modern forms, such as the Almighty’s saying: And they will find what they did present, and His saying: On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and left behind, and And the disbeliever will say, ‘Oh, I wish I were dust,’ meaning, the disbeliever will wish on that day that he had been dust in this world and had never been created or come into existence. This will be when he witnesses the punishment of God and sees his corrupt deeds recorded against him by the hands of the honorable and righteous angels. It has been said that this will only be wished for when God judges between the animals that were in this world and separates between them with His just judgment that does not wrong, to the point that He takes retribution for the hornless sheep from the horned one. When He has finished judging between them, He says to it: Be dust, and it becomes dust. At that moment, the disbeliever will say, Oh, I wish I were dust, meaning I was an animal so I could return to dust. The meaning of this was mentioned in the famous hadith of the trumpet, and there are reports on it from Abu Hurairah, Abdullah ibn Amr, and others. The end of the interpretation of Surat An-Naba. Praise and thanks be to God, and with Him comes success and protection.
